hyps.why: Edge 5 is the only way for node 2 to reach the output, so reviving it with a conv recovers a lot.
Replacing a removed direct edge with a conv adds a whole new path, a larger gain than upgrading an existing op.
Edge 0 feeds node 1 and everything downstream of it, so reconnecting it with a conv is a large gain.
Going from no op to a conv on edge 4 adds capacity and a path, more than swapping one existing op for another.
Edge 2 starts at node 1, which receives nothing when edge 0 is none, so the edit is nearly inert.
Edge 4 starts at node 1, which is dead when edge 0 is none, so the conv adds almost nothing.
Node 2 cannot reach the output without edge 5, so improving edge 2 has little effect.
Edge 1 feeds node 2, which is disconnected from the output when edge 5 is none.
Deleting a 3x3 conv on the direct edge hurts more than deleting a weaker op.
Deleting a conv on the input edge removes a lot of capacity and connectivity.
